user: Why would losing the line Bus_28 -> Bus_29 be critical at 18:00 on 6 January when it was not at 15:00?

assistant:
With the same outage—**Bus_28–Bus_29 [L38]**—Bus_29’s voltage was **0.952 p.u. at 15:00**, just above the **0.950 p.u.** lower limit, but fell to **0.931 p.u. at 18:00**, below it.

The investigation attributes the **0.021 p.u. drop** mainly to higher demand:

- Demand near Bus_29 rose from **10.50 to 12.77 MW**, accounting for **78.4%** of the drop. Bus_29’s own demand explains most of this local contribution.
- Demand elsewhere rose from **218.41 to 265.66 MW**, contributing a further **21.6%**.
- Changes in the five units’ output were effectively ruled out as a cause.

So the outage was not uniquely different at 18:00; the higher system and nearby demand left Bus_29 more vulnerable when that line was lost. The demand explanation held across the reference states checked.
